narrative:
The model predicts an 84% chance that you will leave your job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This high probability means the system sees strong signs that you are likely to depart in the near future.

Three factors stood out most in driving this prediction. First, having received other job opportunities while working here was the strongest influence, pushing the model strongly toward expecting you to leave. Most employees predicted to stay never received such offers, so this factor worked against you. Second, your overall experience of 6-10 years across all jobs also increased the likelihood of leaving. While many who stay have only 1-5 years of total experience, your mid-level experience appears to open more external options. Third, working in the “other” sector rather than medical or education pulled the prediction further toward leaving, as this category is less common among those expected to remain.

These elements together created a clear picture for the model. You might consider discussing your career goals with your manager or exploring internal growth paths that could reduce the appeal of outside offers. The organization should also review how it supports employees at your experience level in non-core sectors to improve retention.
